content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and states its grounds, which is exactly the act the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "'admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings': reading (a) treats this clause as the judge's operative ground for the UNDERDETERMINED verdict, i.e. the single verse states neither the link nor its contrary, which the rule forbids; reading (b) treats it as a non-decisive observation with the verdict resting on the neutralized witness exchange; I chose (a) because the clause immediately follows the verdict marker and the exchange clause only locates each side's answers without weighing any support.", "why": "The judge grounds the UNDERDETERMINED verdict in the fact that the single verse Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, stating neither the link nor its contrary, the very ground K-S2 declares never available."}
